cls: Phosphonic acid antibacterial (cell wall synthesis inhibitor)
quick: With or without food; dissolve in water
Can be used when indicated; data reassuring
Caution if CrCl very low; avoid if severe
Symptom resolution; C. difficile if diarrhea
summary: Fosfomycin tromethamine is a phosphonic acid antibiotic given as a single 3 g oral sachet for uncomplicated urinary tract infection (acute cystitis) in women caused by susceptible E. coli and Enterococcus faecalis. It is bactericidal, inhibiting an early step of cell wall synthesis. It is not for pyelonephritis. Diarrhea is the most common side effect; C. difficile colitis is a class warning.
indications: Uncomplicated urinary tract infection (acute cystitis) in women due to susceptible Escherichia coli and Enterococcus faecalis
Not indicated for pyelonephritis or perinephric abscess

dosage.n: Dissolve in 90-120 mL cold water and drink immediately; do not take dry
Not FDA-approved dosing; guided by culture and ID advice

admin: Pour the entire contents of one sachet into 90-120 mL (3-4 oz) of cold water and stir to dissolve
Drink the solution immediately; do not use hot water and do not take in dry form
May be taken with or without food
A single dose is the complete course for uncomplicated cystitis
moa: Fosfomycin is a bactericidal agent that inactivates the enzyme MurA (UDP-N-acetylglucosamine enolpyruvyl transferase), blocking the first committed step of bacterial cell wall peptidoglycan synthesis. It enters bacteria via glycerophosphate and hexose-6-phosphate transport systems. Its unique target gives a low rate of cross-resistance with other antibiotic classes.

relative: Pyelonephritis or systemic/upper urinary tract infection (not effective)
monitor: Recurrent or persistent bacteriuria after treatment

preg: Animal studies showed fetotoxicity only at maternally toxic doses; human data and clinical experience are reassuring. Single-dose fosfomycin is widely used for cystitis in pregnancy when indicated; use if the benefit justifies use.
lact: It is not known whether fosfomycin is excreted in human milk per the label; a single 3 g dose is generally considered compatible with breastfeeding given low expected infant exposure. Weigh importance of the drug to the mother.
renal: Urinary fosfomycin concentrations fall with declining renal function. Use with caution; it is generally avoided or less effective in severe renal impairment (e.g., CrCl < 10 mL/min).
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment is recommended in hepatic impairment.

moderate: Metoclopramide and other prokinetics that increase GI motility - lower serum and urinary fosfomycin concentrations; avoid coadministration
minor: Cimetidine - no effect on fosfomycin pharmacokinetics
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; food can slightly delay absorption.
interactions.diagnostics: No specific clinically significant laboratory interference.

emergency: Severe or fulminant C. difficile colitis

monitoring: Resolution of cystitis symptoms; reassess if persistence or recurrence of bacteriuria
Diarrhea suggestive of C. difficile during or after therapy
counsel: Mix one sachet in cold water, stir and drink right away; never take it dry
One dose is the full treatment - improvement may take 2-3 days
Contact a clinician if symptoms do not improve, worsen, or if fever or flank pain develops
Report severe or watery/bloody diarrhea, which may occur even weeks later
Avoid metoclopramide around the time of the dose
pk: Absorbed within hours; high urinary levels
pearls: Single 3 g oral dose offers convenience and excellent adherence for uncomplicated cystitis
Active against many multidrug-resistant uropathogens including ESBL-producing E. coli
Not effective for pyelonephritis - reserve for lower UTI only
Prokinetics like metoclopramide reduce fosfomycin urinary levels - separate or avoid
missed: Fosfomycin for cystitis is a single-dose therapy, so there is no second dose to miss. If a prescribed dose was not taken, take it when remembered; do not take extra sachets unless directed by a clinician.
overdose: Reported overdose effects include vestibular loss, impaired hearing, metallic taste and decline in taste perception. There is no specific antidote; treat symptomatically and supportively, with rehydration and clearance of fosfomycin from the urinary tract.
